---
name: task-status
description: What the task status labels mean and how you (the agent) set them — you OWN your task's terminal status via `horizon task set`; the machine only ever leaves it queued/running, so `done` is never inferred from your report or a clean exit.
---

A task is the unit of work a run dispatches. **You own its outcome.** The
orchestrator/scheduler only ever writes `queued` and `running`; it never reads
your report and never marks a task `done`, `blocked`, or `failed` for you. If you
do not record a terminal status, the task simply returns to `queued` for the next
round. Record status through the CLI — invoke it via the `$HORIZON_BIN` env var
(an absolute path); a bare `horizon` may not be on your shell's PATH.

## The labels

- `queued` — runnable. The scheduler picks up only queued tasks. This is where a
  task rests between rounds when work remains. **Set by the machine (and humans);
  you normally don't.**
- `running` — a session is actively driving it right now. **Set by the machine at
  dispatch.** Don't set this yourself — it means "another session is live," and
  the CLI refuses to start a second run of a `running` task.
- `done` — the assigned objective is **FULLY complete**: the Lean is proved and
  builds, the blueprint node(s) are closed, nothing in the objective remains. Not
  "mostly done", not "the hard part is done", not "a clean commit landed". **Only
  you can set this, and only when it is genuinely, completely finished.** A
  reviewer (human or work-reviewer subagent) checks it against the diff and the
  Lean state and will flip a premature `done` back — so a false `done` wastes a
  round, it doesn't save one.
- `blocked` — you cannot make progress: a dependency is missing, a decision is
  needed, or an external constraint stops you. Say why in a comment.
- `failed` — you genuinely could not do the work (not merely "ran out of time" —
  that's just `queued` for next round). Say why in a comment.
- `cancelled` — abandoned by a human. You won't normally set this.

## How to set status

```
"$HORIZON_BIN" task set <task_id> --status done      # objective FULLY complete
"$HORIZON_BIN" task set <task_id> --status blocked   # stuck; explain in a comment
"$HORIZON_BIN" task set <task_id> --status failed    # could not do it; explain
```

Authorship is automatic — the CLI stamps your role (normally `horizon`) from the
run environment; do not pass `--author`. Setting a status appends an auditable
history entry, and if the task has `roadmap_refs` the linked roadmap items are
synced (done→done, blocked/failed→blocked, cancelled→rejected).

Task commands also report advisory queue-health warnings. Review an oversized
open queue for duplicated or roadmap-only objectives, and investigate a task
that has remained `running` past the stale-status window. These warnings never
change status for you; if the state is intentional, it may remain as-is.

## Comment as you work

Leave a short comment only for a durable state change or blocker. Default to one
sentence or at most three bullets: conclusion, evidence, next open obligation.
Do not restate commit summaries, the session report, or earlier comments.

```
"$HORIZON_BIN" task comment <task_id> --body "Closed the base case; representability remains open."
```

## The one rule to remember

**If the objective is only partly advanced, set nothing.** The task returns to
`queued` and the next round continues it. Reserve `done` for work that is
completely finished — that is the entire point of the status now living with you
instead of being guessed from your report.

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0RankOnePresentation
import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Subfunctor.Image

/-!
# The presentation locus for the rank-one Abel map

`PicRankOneOpen` is the functorial locus in the degree-`genus C` Picard layer whose pullback to
every affine test admits a tied `PicRankOneLocalPresentation`.  Quantifying after every affine
pullback makes the condition intrinsic on arbitrary test schemes; stability under further
pullback is exactly `picEtMap_comp`.

The remaining declarations form the corresponding preimages in the widened divisor functor and
in its canonical representing Yoneda functor, together with the restricted Abel transformations.
These are logical subfunctors only.  In particular, this file does not assert that
`PicRankOneOpen` is represented by an open subscheme.  The relative-openness acceptance gate and
the conditional universal-divisor carrier contract are exposed separately in `DivRankOneOpen.lean`.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
variable (pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite pi]

noncomputable section

/-- The rank-one presentation locus in the degree-`genus C` Picard layer.

Membership means that every affine pullback of the input plus class admits a local presentation
tied to that pullback.  This is the correct logical subfunctor underlying the future open Picard
locus; no openness or representability assertion is part of this definition. -/
def PicRankOneOpen :
    Subfunctor (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)) where
  obj T := {lam | ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
      (t : overSpec k A ⟶ T.unop),
    Nonempty (PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi
      ((picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map t.op lam))}
  map {T T'} f lam hlam A _ _ t := by
    let F := picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)
    have e : F.map t.op (F.map f lam) = F.map (t ≫ f.unop).op lam := by
      apply Subtype.ext
      exact (picEtMap_comp C f.unop t lam.1).symm
    rw [e]
    exact hlam A (t ≫ f.unop)

/-! ## The public membership contract -/

/-- The exact producer predicate for the rank-one locus.

This is intentionally lambda-tied and quantifies over every affine pullback.  In particular, it
is stronger than a field-fibre `h⁰ = 1`/`H¹ = 0` statement: a producer must supply the complete
`PicRankOneLocalPresentation` structure for the pulled-back class. -/
def PicRankOneOpen.LocalPresentationCondition
    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
    (lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T) : Prop :=
  ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    (t : overSpec k A ⟶ T.unop),
    Nonempty (PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi
      ((picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map t.op lam))

/-- Unfolded membership in `PicRankOneOpen`, with the presentation tied to the pulled-back
Picard class.  Keeping this predicate named is important for producers in later lanes: a
field-level divisor or chart witness is not a substitute for this arbitrary-affine-pullback
contract. -/
theorem mem_picRankOneOpen_iff {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
    (lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T) :
    lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T ↔
      ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
        (t : overSpec k A ⟶ T.unop),
        Nonempty (PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi
          ((picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map t.op lam)) := by
  rfl

/-- Constructor for the exact lambda-tied arbitrary-affine-pullback presentation contract. -/
theorem mem_picRankOneOpen_of_localPresentations
    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
    {lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T}
    (h : ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
        (t : overSpec k A ⟶ T.unop),
        Nonempty (PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi
          ((picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map t.op lam))) :
    lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T :=
  (mem_picRankOneOpen_iff pi lam).mpr h

/-- Constructor using the named arbitrary-affine producer predicate. -/
theorem mem_picRankOneOpen_of_localPresentationCondition
    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
    {lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T}
    (h : PicRankOneOpen.LocalPresentationCondition pi lam) :
    lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T := by
  exact mem_picRankOneOpen_of_localPresentations pi h

/-- The inclusion of the public rank-one locus into its degree-genus ambient functor. -/
def picRankOneOpenIncl :
    (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor ⟶ picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ) :=
  (PicRankOneOpen pi).ι

/-- The same inclusion after the slice-to-big-site `Σ` extension.

`IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` is a property of presheaves on schemes.  The rank-one functor is
defined on the slice over `Spec k`, so the `Σ` extension is the category-correct carrier for the
relative-open gate below. -/
def picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl :
    Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor ⟶
      Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)) :=
  Over.sigmaExtensionNat (PicRankOneOpen pi).ι

/-- Relative openness of the public locus, in Mathlib's presheaf sense.

This is a named acceptance gate rather than an unproved global assertion.  A future geometric
producer discharges it by supplying the represented open pullbacks; no arbitrary `Subfunctor` is
silently treated as an open subscheme. -/
def PicRankOneOpen.IsOpen : Prop :=
  IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi)

/-- Expose a supplied relative-open certificate without hiding it behind typeclass search. -/
theorem picRankOneOpen_isOpen_of_certificate
    (h : PicRankOneOpen.IsOpen pi) : PicRankOneOpen.IsOpen pi :=
  h

/-- Extract the open immersion supplied by the relative-openness certificate on an arbitrary
pullback.  This is the exact shape consumed by an eventual chart/fibre producer. -/
theorem picRankOneOpen_openPullback
    (h : PicRankOneOpen.IsOpen pi)
    {X Z : Scheme.{u}}
    (g : yoneda.obj X ⟶
      Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)))
    (fst : yoneda.obj Z ⟶
      Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor)
    (snd : Z ⟶ X)
    (hpb : IsPullback fst (yoneda.map snd) (picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi) g) :
    IsOpenImmersion snd :=
  h.property g fst snd hpb

/-- Pullback stability of the public rank-one locus, exposed independently of its definition. -/
theorem picRankOneOpen_map_mem {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
    (f : T ⟶ T') {lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T}
    (h : lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T) :
    (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map f lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T' :=
  (PicRankOneOpen pi).map f h

/-- Pullback stability of the public locus, with the base-change direction made explicit. -/
theorem picRankOneOpen_baseChange_mem {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
    (f : T ⟶ T') {lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T}
    (h : lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T) :
    (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map f lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T' :=
  picRankOneOpen_map_mem pi f h

/-- The inverse image of `PicRankOneOpen` under the affine widened Abel transformation.

This name deliberately records only a presentation-theoretic preimage.  It is not the future
open subscheme `DivRankOneOpen`. -/
def divRankOnePresentationPreimageAff :
    Subfunctor (divFunctorAff C (genus C)) :=
  (PicRankOneOpen pi).preimage (abelDivAffTrans C (genus C))

/-- The same presentation preimage on the Yoneda functor of the canonical genus divisor
representer. -/
def divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter :
    Subfunctor (yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C)) :=
  (divRankOnePresentationPreimageAff pi).preimage
    (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).toIso.hom

/-- The affine Abel transformation restricted to the rank-one presentation preimage. -/
def rankOneAbelAff :
    (divRankOnePresentationPreimageAff pi).toFunctor ⟶
      (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor :=
  (PicRankOneOpen pi).fromPreimage (abelDivAffTrans C (genus C))

/-- Restrict the canonical representation isomorphism to the rank-one presentation preimage. -/
def rankOneRepresenterRestriction :
    (divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter pi).toFunctor ⟶
      (divRankOnePresentationPreimageAff pi).toFunctor :=
  (divRankOnePresentationPreimageAff pi).fromPreimage
    (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).toIso.hom

/-- The represented genus Abel map restricted to the rank-one presentation preimage. -/
def rankOneAbelRepresented :
    (divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter pi).toFunctor ⟶
      (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor :=
  rankOneRepresenterRestriction pi ≫ rankOneAbelAff pi

/-- Immediate consumer theorem: the restricted represented Abel map lands in the public locus.
The stronger canonical inverse still needs the family-level divisor/evaluation producer; this
theorem records the exact target API that consumer lanes can use today. -/
theorem rankOneAbelRepresented_mem {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
    (x : (divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter pi).obj T) :
    ((rankOneAbelRepresented pi).app T x :
      (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T) ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T :=
  ((rankOneAbelRepresented pi).app T x).property

end

end AlgebraicGeometry

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0RankOneLocus
import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Restrict

/-!
# The universal divisor rank-one open contract

The genus divisor representer is unconditional, while the rank-one restriction still needs a
family-level open-locus producer.  This file separates those two facts.  The predicate below is
the inverse image of `PicRankOneOpen` along the represented universal Abel map.  A
`DivRankOneOpenData` witness identifies that predicate with the range of one actual open of the
representer; only after that witness is supplied do we define the open subscheme.

This shape prevents a logical `Subfunctor` from being silently reinterpreted as a scheme.  It also
gives the canonical inverse lane a stable contract: it consumes the witness equality and can use
the resulting open inclusion and all of its pullbacks without choosing a generator.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
variable (pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite pi]

noncomputable section

/-- The universal genus-divisor predicate whose Abel class lies in `PicRankOneOpen`. -/
def divRankOneUniversalPredicate :
    Subfunctor (yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C)) :=
  divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter pi

/-- The Yoneda map induced by the inclusion of an open of an object in the slice.  Naming this
map is useful to consumers which need the actual factorisation through the open, rather than only
the proposition that a point lies in its range. -/
def openSubfunctorMap (D : Over (Spec (.of k))) (U : D.left.Opens) :
    yoneda.obj (Over.mk (U.ι ≫ D.hom)) ⟶ yoneda.obj D :=
  yoneda.map (Over.homMk (U := Over.mk (U.ι ≫ D.hom)) U.ι)

/-- The subfunctor represented by an open `U` of an object `D` in the slice over `Spec k`.

Its values are precisely morphisms which factor through the open immersion `U.ι`; using the
Yoneda range keeps this definition independent of any chosen affine presentation of `U`. -/
def openSubfunctor (D : Over (Spec (.of k))) (U : D.left.Opens) :
    Subfunctor (yoneda.obj D) :=
  Subfunctor.range (openSubfunctorMap D U)

/-- Unpack range membership into the actual source point and its equality in the ambient Yoneda
functor.  This is the pointwise factorisation API used by inverse constructions. -/
theorem openSubfunctor_mem_iff
    (D : Over (Spec (.of k))) (U : D.left.Opens)
    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
    (x : (yoneda.obj D).obj T) :
    x ∈ (openSubfunctor D U).obj T ↔
      ∃ y : (yoneda.obj (Over.mk (U.ι ≫ D.hom))).obj T,
        (openSubfunctorMap D U).app T y = x := by
  rfl

/-- An explicit geometric certificate for the universal rank-one predicate.

The equality is the missing family-level producer/gluing statement: it identifies the logical
preimage with an actual open of the canonical genus representer.  No default or top-open witness
is manufactured here. -/
structure DivRankOneOpenData (pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite pi] where
  carrier : (divRepAffGenusScheme C).left.Opens
  carrier_eq :
    openSubfunctor (divRepAffGenusScheme C) carrier =
      divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi

/-- The open subscheme supplied by a `DivRankOneOpenData` witness. -/
def DivRankOneOpen (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi) : Scheme :=
  h.carrier.toScheme

/-- The canonical open immersion into the genus divisor representer. -/
def divRankOneOpenMap (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi) :
    DivRankOneOpen pi h ⟶ (divRepAffGenusScheme C).left :=
  h.carrier.ι

theorem divRankOneOpen_isOpenImmersion
    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi) :
    IsOpenImmersion (divRankOneOpenMap pi h) := by
  change IsOpenImmersion h.carrier.ι
  infer_instance

/-- The open represented object, retained in the slice over `Spec k` for consumers of the affine
divisor functor. -/
def divRankOneOpenOver (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi) :
    Over (Spec (.of k)) :=
  Over.mk (divRankOneOpenMap pi h ≫ (divRepAffGenusScheme C).hom)

/-- Pull back the certified rank-one open along an arbitrary slice morphism. -/
def divRankOneOpenPullback
    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi)
    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (q : T ⟶ divRepAffGenusScheme C) : T.left.Opens :=
  q.left ⁻¹ᵁ h.carrier

theorem divRankOneOpenPullback_isOpenImmersion
    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi)
    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (q : T ⟶ divRepAffGenusScheme C) :
    IsOpenImmersion (divRankOneOpenPullback pi h q).ι := by
  infer_instance

/-- Pointwise form of arbitrary base-change compatibility for the certified open. -/
theorem mem_divRankOneOpenPullback_iff
    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi)
    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (q : T ⟶ divRepAffGenusScheme C)
    (x : T.left) :
    x ∈ divRankOneOpenPullback pi h q ↔ q.left.base x ∈ h.carrier := by
  rfl

/-- The universal predicate is exactly the represented preimage used by the Abel restriction. -/
theorem divRankOneUniversalPredicate_eq_preimage :
    divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi = divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter pi :=
  rfl

/-- The certified open carrier has the universal rank-one predicate as its Yoneda range. -/
theorem divRankOneOpen_carrier_eq
    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi) :
    openSubfunctor (divRepAffGenusScheme C) h.carrier =
      divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi :=
  h.carrier_eq

/-- Pointwise form of the witness equality, exposing the exact contract consumed by an inverse.

The right-hand side is the range of the open immersion, so a consumer can use this theorem to
replace a rank-one predicate proof by a factorisation through `DivRankOneOpen pi h`. -/
theorem divRankOneOpen_mem_iff
    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi)
    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
    (x : (yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C)).obj T) :
    x ∈ (divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi).obj T ↔
      x ∈ (openSubfunctor (divRepAffGenusScheme C) h.carrier).obj T := by
  rw [h.carrier_eq]

/-- A point of the universal rank-one predicate factors through the certified open immersion.

Unlike a bare range-membership proof, the conclusion exposes the source point and the equality
of its image with the given divisor point, which is the exact data needed by a canonical inverse. -/
theorem divRankOneOpen_mem_iff_factorization
    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi)
    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
    (x : (yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C)).obj T) :
    x ∈ (divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi).obj T ↔
      ∃ y : (yoneda.obj (Over.mk
          (h.carrier.ι ≫ (divRepAffGenusScheme C).hom))).obj T,
        (openSubfunctorMap (divRepAffGenusScheme C) h.carrier).app T y = x := by
  rw [divRankOneOpen_mem_iff pi h x, openSubfunctor_mem_iff]

/-- A point in the certified open carrier is a point of the universal rank-one predicate. -/
theorem divRankOneOpen_mem_of_carrier
    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi)
    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
    {x : (yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C)).obj T}
    (hx : x ∈ (openSubfunctor (divRepAffGenusScheme C) h.carrier).obj T) :
    x ∈ (divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi).obj T := by
  exact (divRankOneOpen_mem_iff pi h x).mpr hx

/- The logical rank-one predicate remains stable under arbitrary pullback, independently of the
   geometric witness used to represent it by an open. -/
theorem divRankOneOpen_baseChange_mem
    {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
    (f : T ⟶ T')
    {x : (yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C)).obj T}
    (hx : x ∈ (divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi).obj T) :
    (yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C)).map f x ∈
      (divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi).obj T' :=
  (divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi).map f hx

end

This is the geometric wrapper around `RankOneFibre`: the genuine chart-reading ideal is mapped
to `B/(read s)`, and that image is definitionally `chartIdealColengthModule`.  Thus a pointwise
span statement for the fibre of the ideal immediately gives the desired vanishing of the
colength fibre.  The span statement is allowed to include the zero-fibre case.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false

universe u

open CategoryTheory TopologicalSpace Opposite
open scoped TensorProduct

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π] {a : ℕ}

namespace ThetaGeneratorSeed

/-- **Pointwise chart-colength fibre vanishing from ideal-fibre span.**  Let `B` be the
pinned-chart section ring, `J` the genuine `B`-ideal generated by the readings of `K`, and
`I = (read s)` for `s ∈ K`.  If every vector of
`κ(p) ⊗[B] J` is a scalar multiple of `1 ⊗ read(s)`, then the image of `J` in `B/I` has
zero `κ(p)`-fibre.  This is the exact single-point input consumed by the `κ(z)` RD-N bridge;
it uses no global base-fibre or flatness inference. -/
theorem subsingleton_chartIdealColengthModule_tensor_residueField_of_ideal_span
    (K : Submodule R (relThetaSections C R π a)) (b : Bool)
    (s : relThetaSections C R π a) (hsK : s ∈ K)
    (p : PrimeSpectrum Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b))
    (hspan : ∀ v : p.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[
        Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b)]
        (chartReadIdeal K b), ∃ c : p.asIdeal.ResidueField,
          c • ((1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ⊗ₜ[
            Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b)]
            (⟨relThetaResSide a b (le_rfl) s,
              by
                exact Ideal.subset_span ⟨⟨s, hsK⟩, rfl⟩⟩ :
              chartReadIdeal K b)) = v) :
    Subsingleton ((chartIdealColengthModule K b s) ⊗[
      Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b)] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) := by
  let B : Type u := Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b)
  let I : Ideal B := Ideal.span {relThetaResSide a b le_rfl s}
  let P : Submodule B B := chartReadIdeal K b
  let f : B →ₗ[B] (B ⧸ I) := (Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ B I).toLinearMap
  have hsP : relThetaResSide a b le_rfl s ∈ P := by
    exact Ideal.subset_span ⟨⟨s, hsK⟩, rfl⟩
  have hfs : f (relThetaResSide a b le_rfl s) = 0 := by
    change Ideal.Quotient.mk I (relThetaResSide a b le_rfl s) = 0
    exact Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem.mpr (Ideal.subset_span (by simp))
  have hzero := RankOneFibre.subsingleton_map_tensor_of_span_singleton
    P f (relThetaResSide a b le_rfl s) hsP (by
      · intro v
        exact hspan v) (by
      · exact hfs)
  change Subsingleton ((P.map f) ⊗[B] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) at hzero
  exact hzero

end ThetaGeneratorSeed

end AlgebraicGeometry

import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.FiniteDimensional.Basic
import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.TensorProduct.RightExactness

/-!
# Rank-one fibre quotients

If a vector `1 ⊗ s` is nonzero in a one-dimensional fibre `K ⊗[B] M`, then it spans that
fibre.  Consequently, every surjective image of `M` that kills `s` has zero `K`-fibre.

The mapped-submodule form is tailored to an ideal `J ≤ B`: if the fibre of `J` has rank one,
`s ∈ J` survives in that fibre, and a quotient map kills `s`, then the image of `J` in the
quotient has zero residue-field fibre.  This is purely right exactness of tensor product;
neither flatness nor finite generation over `B` is needed at this step.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open scoped TensorProduct

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

namespace RankOneFibre

/-- A surjective image has zero field fibre when every source-fibre vector is a scalar multiple
of `1 ⊗ s`, and the image kills `s`.  The spanning hypothesis also covers the zero-fibre case;
no dimension or nonzero-vector assumption is required. -/
theorem subsingleton_tensor_of_surjective_of_span_singleton
    {B K M N : Type u} [CommRing B] [Field K] [Algebra B K]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module B N]
    (f : M →ₗ[B] N) (hf : Function.Surjective f) (s : M)
    (hspan : ∀ v : K ⊗[B] M, ∃ c : K, c • ((1 : K) ⊗ₜ[B] s) = v)
    (hfs : f s = 0) :
    Subsingleton (N ⊗[B] K) := by
  have hft : Function.Surjective (f.lTensor K) :=
    LinearMap.lTensor_surjective K hf
  have hzero : ∀ v : K ⊗[B] M, (f.lTensor K) v = 0 := by
    intro v
    obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := hspan v
    rw [← hc, ← TensorProduct.tmul_eq_smul_one_tmul c s,
      LinearMap.lTensor_tmul, hfs]
    simp
  have hsub : Subsingleton (K ⊗[B] N) := by
    refine ⟨fun x y => ?_⟩
    obtain ⟨x', rfl⟩ := hft x
    obtain ⟨y', rfl⟩ := hft y
    rw [hzero x', hzero y']
  exact (TensorProduct.comm B N K).toEquiv.subsingleton

/-- A surjective image of a module has zero field fibre if it kills a nonzero vector spanning
the one-dimensional source fibre. -/
theorem subsingleton_tensor_of_surjective_of_finrank_eq_one
    {B K M N : Type u} [CommRing B] [Field K] [Algebra B K]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module B N]
    (f : M →ₗ[B] N) (hf : Function.Surjective f) (s : M)
    (hfin : Module.finrank K (K ⊗[B] M) = 1)
    (hs : (1 : K) ⊗ₜ[B] s ≠ 0) (hfs : f s = 0) :
    Subsingleton (N ⊗[B] K) := by
  apply subsingleton_tensor_of_surjective_of_span_singleton f hf s
  intro v
  exact exists_smul_eq_of_finrank_eq_one hfin hs v
  exact hfs

/-- If a linear map kills a generator of a one-dimensional source fibre, the fibre of its
range is zero. -/
theorem subsingleton_range_tensor_of_finrank_eq_one
    {B K M N : Type u} [CommRing B] [Field K] [Algebra B K]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module B N]
    (f : M →ₗ[B] N) (s : M)
    (hfin : Module.finrank K (K ⊗[B] M) = 1)
    (hs : (1 : K) ⊗ₜ[B] s ≠ 0) (hfs : f s = 0) :
    Subsingleton ((LinearMap.range f) ⊗[B] K) := by
  apply subsingleton_tensor_of_surjective_of_finrank_eq_one f.rangeRestrict
    (LinearMap.surjective_rangeRestrict f) s hfin hs
  apply Subtype.ext
  exact hfs

/-- Range specialization of `subsingleton_tensor_of_surjective_of_span_singleton`. -/
theorem subsingleton_range_tensor_of_span_singleton
    {B K M N : Type u} [CommRing B] [Field K] [Algebra B K]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module B N]
    (f : M →ₗ[B] N) (s : M)
    (hspan : ∀ v : K ⊗[B] M, ∃ c : K, c • ((1 : K) ⊗ₜ[B] s) = v)
    (hfs : f s = 0) :
    Subsingleton ((LinearMap.range f) ⊗[B] K) := by
  apply subsingleton_tensor_of_surjective_of_span_singleton f.rangeRestrict
    (LinearMap.surjective_rangeRestrict f) s hspan
  apply Subtype.ext
  exact hfs

/-- Let `P` be a submodule whose field fibre is one-dimensional.  If `s ∈ P` survives in
that fibre and `f s = 0`, then the fibre of the image `f(P)` is zero.

For a chart ideal `J` and the quotient map `B → B/(s)`, the conclusion is precisely the
vanishing of the fibre of the image of `J` in `B/(s)`. -/
theorem subsingleton_map_tensor_of_finrank_eq_one
    {B K M N : Type u} [CommRing B] [Field K] [Algebra B K]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module B N]
    (P : Submodule B M) (f : M →ₗ[B] N) (s : M) (hsP : s ∈ P)
    (hfin : Module.finrank K (K ⊗[B] P) = 1)
    (hs : (1 : K) ⊗ₜ[B] (⟨s, hsP⟩ : P) ≠ 0) (hfs : f s = 0) :
    Subsingleton ((P.map f) ⊗[B] K) := by
  rw [← LinearMap.range_domRestrict P f]
  apply subsingleton_range_tensor_of_finrank_eq_one
    (f.domRestrict P) (⟨s, hsP⟩ : P) hfin hs
  simpa using hfs

/-- Mapped-submodule specialization of `subsingleton_tensor_of_surjective_of_span_singleton`.
This is useful when the source ideal fibre may itself be zero. -/
theorem subsingleton_map_tensor_of_span_singleton
    {B K M N : Type u} [CommRing B] [Field K] [Algebra B K]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module B N]
    (P : Submodule B M) (f : M →ₗ[B] N) (s : M) (hsP : s ∈ P)
    (hspan : ∀ v : K ⊗[B] P, ∃ c : K,
      c • ((1 : K) ⊗ₜ[B] (⟨s, hsP⟩ : P)) = v) (hfs : f s = 0) :
    Subsingleton ((P.map f) ⊗[B] K) := by
  rw [← LinearMap.range_domRestrict P f]
  apply subsingleton_range_tensor_of_span_singleton
    (f.domRestrict P) (⟨s, hsP⟩ : P) hspan
  simpa using hfs

/-- Quotienting by a vector that survives and spans a one-dimensional field fibre produces
a quotient with zero field fibre. -/
theorem subsingleton_quotient_span_tensor_of_finrank_eq_one
    {B K M : Type u} [CommRing B] [Field K] [Algebra B K]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M]
    (s : M) (hfin : Module.finrank K (K ⊗[B] M) = 1)
    (hs : (1 : K) ⊗ₜ[B] s ≠ 0) :
    Subsingleton ((M ⧸ Submodule.span B ({s} : Set M)) ⊗[B] K) := by
  apply subsingleton_tensor_of_surjective_of_finrank_eq_one
    (Submodule.span B ({s} : Set M)).mkQ
    (Submodule.mkQ_surjective _) s hfin hs
  rw [Submodule.mkQ_apply, Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero]
  exact Submodule.mem_span_singleton_self s

end RankOneFibre

end AlgebraicGeometry

    10	# The presentation locus for the rank-one Abel map
    11	
    12	`PicRankOneOpen` is the functorial locus in the degree-`genus C` Picard layer whose pullback to
    13	every affine test admits a tied `PicRankOneLocalPresentation`.  Quantifying after every affine
    14	pullback makes the condition intrinsic on arbitrary test schemes; stability under further
    15	pullback is exactly `picEtMap_comp`.
    16	
    17	The remaining declarations form the corresponding preimages in the widened divisor functor and
    18	in its canonical representing Yoneda functor, together with the restricted Abel transformations.
    19	These are logical subfunctors only.  In particular, this file does not assert that
    20	`PicRankOneOpen` is represented by an open subscheme.  The relative-openness acceptance gate and
    21	the conditional universal-divisor carrier contract are exposed separately in `DivRankOneOpen.lean`.
    22	-/

    24	set_option autoImplicit false
    25	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

    32

    34	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    35	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    36	variable (pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite pi]
    37	
    38	noncomputable section
    39	
    40	/-- The rank-one presentation locus in the degree-`genus C` Picard layer.
    41	
    42	Membership means that every affine pullback of the input plus class admits a local presentation
    43	tied to that pullback.  This is the correct logical subfunctor underlying the future open Picard
    44	locus; no openness or representability assertion is part of this definition. -/
    45	def PicRankOneOpen :
    46	    Subfunctor (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)) where
    47	  obj T := {lam | ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    48	      (t : overSpec k A ⟶ T.unop),
    49	    Nonempty (PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi
    50	      ((picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map t.op lam))}
    51	  map {T T'} f lam hlam A _ _ t := by
    52	    let F := picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)
    53	    have e : F.map t.op (F.map f lam) = F.map (t ≫ f.unop).op lam := by
    54	      apply Subtype.ext
    55	      exact (picEtMap_comp C f.unop t lam.1).symm
    56	    rw [e]
    57	    exact hlam A (t ≫ f.unop)
    58	
    59	/-! ## The public membership contract -/
    60	
    61	/-- The exact producer predicate for the rank-one locus.
    62	
    63	This is intentionally lambda-tied and quantifies over every affine pullback.  In particular, it
    64	is stronger than a field-fibre `h⁰ = 1`/`H¹ = 0` statement: a producer must supply the complete
    65	`PicRankOneLocalPresentation` structure for the pulled-back class. -/
    66	def PicRankOneOpen.LocalPresentationCondition
    67	    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
    68	    (lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T) : Prop :=
    69	  ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    70	    (t : overSpec k A ⟶ T.unop),
    71	    Nonempty (PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi
    72	      ((picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map t.op lam))
    73	
    74	/-- Unfolded membership in `PicRankOneOpen`, with the presentation tied to the pulled-back
    75	Picard class.  Keeping this predicate named is important for producers in later lanes: a
    76	field-level divisor or chart witness is not a substitute for this arbitrary-affine-pullback
    77	contract. -/
    78	theorem mem_picRankOneOpen_iff {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
    79	    (lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T) :
    80	    lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T ↔
    81	      ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    82	        (t : overSpec k A ⟶ T.unop),
    83	        Nonempty (PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi
    84	          ((picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map t.op lam)) := by
    85	  rfl

    87	/-- Constructor for the exact lambda-tied arbitrary-affine-pullback presentation contract. -/
    88	theorem mem_picRankOneOpen_of_localPresentations
    89	    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
    90	    {lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T}
    91	    (h : ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    92	        (t : overSpec k A ⟶ T.unop),
    93	        Nonempty (PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi
    94	          ((picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map t.op lam))) :
    95	    lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T :=
    96	  (mem_picRankOneOpen_iff pi lam).mpr h
    97	
    98	/-- Constructor using the named arbitrary-affine producer predicate. -/
    99	theorem mem_picRankOneOpen_of_localPresentationCondition
   100	    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
   101	    {lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T}
   102	    (h : PicRankOneOpen.LocalPresentationCondition pi lam) :
   103	    lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T := by
   104	  exact mem_picRankOneOpen_of_localPresentations pi h

   106	/-- The inclusion of the public rank-one locus into its degree-genus ambient functor. -/
   107	def picRankOneOpenIncl :
   108	    (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor ⟶ picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ) :=
   109	  (PicRankOneOpen pi).ι

   111	/-- The same inclusion after the slice-to-big-site `Σ` extension.
   112	
   113	`IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` is a property of presheaves on schemes.  The rank-one functor is
   114	defined on the slice over `Spec k`, so the `Σ` extension is the category-correct carrier for the
   115	relative-open gate below. -/
   116	def picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl :
   117	    Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor ⟶
   118	      Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)) :=
   119	  Over.sigmaExtensionNat (PicRankOneOpen pi).ι

   123	This is a named acceptance gate rather than an unproved global assertion.  A future geometric
   124	producer discharges it by supplying the represented open pullbacks; no arbitrary `Subfunctor` is

   126	def PicRankOneOpen.IsOpen : Prop :=

   129	/-- Expose a supplied relative-open certificate without hiding it behind typeclass search. -/
   130	theorem picRankOneOpen_isOpen_of_certificate

   133	
   134	/-- Extract the open immersion supplied by the relative-openness certificate on an arbitrary
   135	pullback.  This is the exact shape consumed by an eventual chart/fibre producer. -/
   136	theorem picRankOneOpen_openPullback
   137	    (h : PicRankOneOpen.IsOpen pi)
   138	    {X Z : Scheme.{u}}
   139	    (g : yoneda.obj X ⟶
   140	      Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)))

   144	    (hpb : IsPullback fst (yoneda.map snd) (picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi) g) :

   147	
   148	/-- Pullback stability of the public rank-one locus, exposed independently of its definition. -/
   149	theorem picRankOneOpen_map_mem {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
   150	    (f : T ⟶ T') {lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T}
   151	    (h : lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T) :
   152	    (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map f lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T' :=

   154

   156	theorem picRankOneOpen_baseChange_mem {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
   157	    (f : T ⟶ T') {lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T}

   161	
   162	/-- The inverse image of `PicRankOneOpen` under the affine widened Abel transformation.
   163	
   164	This name deliberately records only a presentation-theoretic preimage.  It is not the future
   165	open subscheme `DivRankOneOpen`. -/
   166	def divRankOnePresentationPreimageAff :
   167	    Subfunctor (divFunctorAff C (genus C)) :=
   168	  (PicRankOneOpen pi).preimage (abelDivAffTrans C (genus C))
   169	
   170	/-- The same presentation preimage on the Yoneda functor of the canonical genus divisor
   171	representer. -/
   172	def divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter :
   173	    Subfunctor (yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C)) :=

   178	def rankOneAbelAff :

   186	      (divRankOnePresentationPreimageAff pi).toFunctor :=

   188	    (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).toIso.hom
   189	
   190	/-- The represented genus Abel map restricted to the rank-one presentation preimage. -/
   191	def rankOneAbelRepresented :
   192	    (divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter pi).toFunctor ⟶
   193	      (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor :=
   194	  rankOneRepresenterRestriction pi ≫ rankOneAbelAff pi

   196	/-- Immediate consumer theorem: the restricted represented Abel map lands in the public locus.
   197	The stronger canonical inverse still needs the family-level divisor/evaluation producer; this

   199	theorem rankOneAbelRepresented_mem {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
   200	    (x : (divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter pi).obj T) :
   201	    ((rankOneAbelRepresented pi).app T x :
   202	      (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T) ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T :=
   203	  ((rankOneAbelRepresented pi).app T x).property

     9	/-!
    10	# The universal divisor rank-one open contract
    11	
    12	The genus divisor representer is unconditional, while the rank-one restriction still needs a
    13	family-level open-locus producer.  This file separates those two facts.  The predicate below is
    14	the inverse image of `PicRankOneOpen` along the represented universal Abel map.  A
    15	`DivRankOneOpenData` witness identifies that predicate with the range of one actual open of the
    16	representer; only after that witness is supplied do we define the open subscheme.
    17	
    18	This shape prevents a logical `Subfunctor` from being silently reinterpreted as a scheme.  It also
    19	gives the canonical inverse lane a stable contract: it consumes the witness equality and can use
    20	the resulting open inclusion and all of its pullbacks without choosing a generator.
    21	-/
    22	
    23	set_option autoImplicit false
    24	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    25	
    26	universe u
    27	
    28	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite
    29	
    30	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    31	
    32	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    33	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    34	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    35	variable (pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite pi]
    36

   114	object the extension is an **isomorphism** (`Over.testPointField_fromSpecAffine_isIso` — hence in
   115	particular separable), so morally transport (i) is free here.
   116	
   117	**But the landed invariance is about `HasWitnessH1Vanishing`, not about `IsSplitWitness`**, and no
   118	declaration in the tree transports `IsSplitWitness` along a field isomorphism: measured, the only
   119	mentions of `IsSplitWitness` invariance are two docstring sentences.  So the affine-piece case of
   120	transport (i) needs *one* lemma the tree does not have, which is this predicate.  That is a
   121	correction to `Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen`'s claim that the general-test statement "needs no new
   122	mathematics": it needs exactly this, and nothing else.
   123	
   124	Why it is believable and small: `IsSplitWitness C μ` is an existential over a finite separable
   125	`L/K` presenting `μ`.  Along an isomorphism `K ≃ K'` the same `L` presents the transported class,
   126	because `PicEtAff.map` composes (`PicEtAff.map_map`) and the inverse iso undoes the transport —
   127	i.e. it is `map_map` plus `map_id`, not geometry.  It is stated as a class-free hypothesis here so
   128	that the assembly below is usable the moment a lane proves it. -/
   129	def IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant : Prop :=
   130	  ∀ (T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))) (f : T' ⟶ T) (t : T'.left)
   131	    (_ : IsIso (Over.testPointFieldMap f t)) (mu : picEt C T),
   132	      IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) (picEtMap C f mu))
   133	        ↔ IsSplitWitness C
   134	            (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint (T := T) (f.left.base t)) mu)
   135	
   136	variable (C) in
   137	/-- **The split-witness predicate agrees along an affine-open test object**, given the
   138	iso-invariance.
   139	
   140	This is transport (i) of `w4-datb` §1.6 for the affine-piece maps, in **both** directions — so
   141	the locus over the piece and the locus over `T` correspond exactly, which is what the locality
   142	assembly needs (a one-sided containment would not give openness).
   143	
   144	The only input beyond landed material is `hinv`; the `IsIso` it is applied at is discharged by
   145	`Over.testPointField_fromSpecAffine_isIso`, i.e. structurally, by mathlib's fact that an open
   146	immersion induces an isomorphism of residue fields. -/
   147	theorem isSplitWitness_fromSpecAffine_iff (hinv : IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant C)
   148	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (U : T.left.affineOpens) (mu : picEt C T)
   149	    (t : (overSpec k Γ(T.left, U.1)).left) :
   150	    IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t)
   151	        (picEtMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) mu))
   152	      ↔ IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C
   153	          (Over.testPoint (T := T) ((Over.fromSpecAffine T U).left.base t)) mu) :=
   154	  hinv T (overSpec k Γ(T.left, U.1)) (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) t
   155	    (Over.testPointField_fromSpecAffine_isIso T U t) mu
   156	
   157	/-! ## Locality: the general-test assembly -/
   158	
   159	variable (C) in
   160	/-- **The affine piece's locus is the preimage of the general-test locus.**
   161	
   162	For an affine open `U ⊆ T.left`, `chartLocus` over the affine test object `Spec Γ(T.left, U)` is
   163	the preimage, along the carrier map of `Over.fromSpecAffine T U`, of `chartLocus` over `T`.
   164	
   165	Both sides unfold to the same split-witness condition read at two residue fields, so this is
   166	`isSplitWitness_fromSpecAffine_iff` applied pointwise together with `picEtMap_chartTwist` (the
   167	twist commutes with restriction). -/
   168	theorem chartLocus_fromSpecAffine_eq_preimage (hinv : IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant C)
   169	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
   170	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (U : T.left.affineOpens) (lam : picEt C T) :
   171	    chartLocus C m Z (picEtMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) lam)
   172	      = (Over.fromSpecAffine T U).left.base ⁻¹' chartLocus C m Z lam := by
   173	  refine Set.ext fun t => ?_
   174	  rw [Set.mem_preimage, mem_chartLocus_iff, mem_chartLocus_iff,
   175	    ← picEtMap_chartTwist]
   176	  exact isSplitWitness_fromSpecAffine_iff C hinv T U (chartTwist C m Z T lam) t
   177	
   178	variable (C) in
   179	/-- **CHART-U(b) AT A GENERAL TEST**, i.e. the statement `Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen`'s docstring
   180	promises follows from the affine case "by the affine-piece locality of the (b-amendment)'s
   181	transport (iii)".
   182	
   183	If `chartLocus` is open over every affine-open test object of `T`, it is open over `T`.
   184	
   185	The bookkeeping is genuinely bookkeeping — but note *which* bookkeeping, because it is not the
   186	`isOpen_iff_forall_isOpen_inter` the docstring names: the piece's locus lives in a **different
   187	space** (`Spec Γ(T.left, U)`, not `T.left`), so the bridge is that the carrier map is an open
   188	immersion whose range is `U` (`IsAffineOpen.range_fromSpec`).  The preimage identity
   189	`chartLocus_fromSpecAffine_eq_preimage` then turns per-piece openness into openness of
   190	`chartLocus ∩ U`, and the affine opens cover `T.left`. -/
   191	theorem isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal (hinv : IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant C)
   192	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
   193	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (lam : picEt C T)
   194	    (haff : ∀ U : T.left.affineOpens,
   195	      IsOpen (chartLocus C m Z (picEtMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) lam))) :
   196	    IsOpen (chartLocus C m Z lam) := by
   197	  -- Openness is local: it suffices that every point of the locus has an open neighbourhood
   198	  -- inside it, and each point lies in some affine open of `T.left`.
   199	  rw [isOpen_iff_forall_mem_open]
   200	  intro t ht
   201	  -- an affine open around `t`
   202	  obtain ⟨U, hUmem⟩ : ∃ U : T.left.affineOpens, t ∈ U.1 := by
   203	    obtain ⟨U, hU, hmem, -⟩ :=
   204	      (TopologicalSpace.Opens.isBasis_iff_nbhd.mp T.left.isBasis_affineOpens)
   205	        (show t ∈ (⊤ : T.left.Opens) from trivial)
   206	    exact ⟨⟨U, hU⟩, hmem⟩
   207	  -- the piece's locus is open, and its image is `chartLocus ∩ U`
   208	  have hpre := chartLocus_fromSpecAffine_eq_preimage C hinv m Z T U lam
   209	  refine ⟨chartLocus C m Z lam ∩ U.1, Set.inter_subset_left, ?_, ht, hUmem⟩
   210	  -- `chartLocus ∩ U` is the image of the piece's locus under an open immersion with range `U`
   211	  have hoi : IsOpenImmersion (Over.fromSpecAffine T U).left := U.2.isOpenImmersion_fromSpec
   212	  have hrange : Set.range (Over.fromSpecAffine T U).left.base = (U.1 : Set T.left) := by
   213	    change Set.range (U.2.fromSpec).base = _
   214	    exact U.2.range_fromSpec
   215	  have himg : (Over.fromSpecAffine T U).left.base ''
   216	        (chartLocus C m Z (picEtMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) lam))
   217	      = chartLocus C m Z lam ∩ U.1 := by
   218	    rw [hpre, Set.image_preimage_eq_inter_range, hrange]
   219	  rw [← himg]
   220	  haveI := hoi
   221	  exact (Over.fromSpecAffine T U).left.isOpenEmbedding.isOpenMap _ (haff U)
   222	
   223	end

   155	/-- **The shifted-datum presentation hypothesis** — the one link of the CHART-U(b) route of

   162	
   163	Two remarks on the shape, both deliberate:
   164	
   165	* it is stated as an **agreement of predicates at every point**, not as a class equality.
   166	  That is weaker than "the datum's class is `μ`", and it is all the openness argument
   167	  consumes — which matters, because the class equality is what needs `cechPicClass_inv` and

   178	def IsChartDatumPresentation {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
   179	    (μ : picEt C (overSpec k A)) (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π) : Prop :=
   180	  ∀ t : (overSpec k A).left,
   181	    D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t)
   182	      ↔ IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) μ)
   183	
   184	/-! ## The carrier translation: `testPointField` on `Spec A` versus `Ideal.ResidueField`
   185	
   186	The engine's open set lives in `PrimeSpectrum A` and is indexed by `q.asIdeal.ResidueField`;
   187	`chartLocus` lives in `(overSpec k A).left = Spec A` and is indexed by `Over.testPointField`.
   188	The two carriers are the same space, but the two *fields* are only canonically isomorphic
   189	(mathlib's `Spec.residueFieldIso`), so the witness predicate has to be carried across that
   190	isomorphism.  That is what this section does, and it is the transport the (b-amendment) folds
   191	into "affine pieces glue by (V1c)-style locality". -/
   192	
   193	/-- **The residue-field comparison at a point of an affine test, as an algebra map.**
   194	
   195	`Over.testPointField t` is the *scheme* residue field `(Spec A).residueField t`, while every
   196	engine-facing predicate reads the *algebraic* residue field `t.asIdeal.ResidueField` of the
   197	prime.  Mathlib's `Spec.residueFieldIso` identifies them; this records the identification in
   198	the form the tower needs, namely that the canonical `A`-algebra structure on the scheme
   199	residue field (`Over.instAlgebraTestPointFieldAffine`) factors through the algebraic one.
   200	
   201	Proof: both sides are `Spec.preimage` of a morphism out of `Spec κ(t)`, and `Spec.map` is
   202	injective on homs, so it suffices to compare after applying `Spec.map` — where the identity is
   203	mathlib's `Spec.map_residueFieldIso_inv_eq_fromSpecResidueField`. -/
   204	lemma algebraMap_testPointFieldAffine_factors {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
   205	    (t : (overSpec k A).left) :
   206	    algebraMap A (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t)
   207	      = ((Scheme.Spec.residueFieldIso (.of A) t).inv).hom.comp
   208	          (algebraMap A (t : PrimeSpectrum A).asIdeal.ResidueField) := by
   209	  rw [Over.algebraMap_testPointFieldAffine]
   210	  have h : Spec.preimage ((overSpec k A).left.fromSpecResidueField t)
   211	      = CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A (t : PrimeSpectrum A).asIdeal.ResidueField)
   212	          ≫ (Scheme.Spec.residueFieldIso (.of A) t).inv := by
   213	    apply Spec.map_injective
   214	    rw [Spec.map_preimage, Spec.map_comp]
   215	    exact (Scheme.Spec.map_residueFieldIso_inv_eq_fromSpecResidueField (.of A) t).symm
   216	  rw [h]
   217	  rfl
   218	
   219	/-- **The witness predicate at a scheme-residue field agrees with the one at the prime's
   220	residue field, and the resulting locus is open.**
   221	
   222	`Over.testPointField t` is `(Spec A).residueField t` and the engine reads
   223	`t.asIdeal.ResidueField`; `Spec.residueFieldIso` identifies them, and the witness predicate
   224	transfers along any field extension in the `A`-tower
   225	(`hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension`, `Pic0ChartLocusFibreField.lean:142`), in
   226	particular along an isomorphism.
   227	
   228	Three points about the proof, each of which was a suspected wall and is not:
   229	
   230	* the **carrier identification** `↥(overSpec k A).left = PrimeSpectrum A` is *definitional*
   231	  (`Scheme.Spec`'s carrier is `PrimeSpectrum` on the nose), so the two index sets need no
   232	  transport and the two topologies agree by `rfl`.  The set equality below is therefore a
   233	  pointwise `Iff`, not a homeomorphism argument;
   234	* the `Algebra A (testPointField t)` and `IsScalarTower k A (testPointField t)` instances the
   235	  predicate needs are **already canonical** (`Over.instAlgebraTestPointFieldAffine`,
   236	  `Over.instIsScalarTowerTestPointFieldAffine`), so nothing has to be passed in as an
   237	  argument.  An earlier draft of this file took `alg`/`tow` as explicit hypotheses and left
   238	  the conclusion as a `sorry`; that was a statement-shape artifact, not a gap — and worse,
   239	  the hypothesis form is *false for some regradings*, since an arbitrary `alg` need not be the
   240	  canonical instance and the predicate is not invariant under regrading the field over `A`;
   241	* the only genuine content is the transport across `Spec.residueFieldIso`, which is
   242	  `hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension` applied to the isomorphism, in the tower
   243	  `A → κ(q) → (Spec A).residueField t` supplied by
   244	  `algebraMap_testPointFieldAffine_factors`. -/
   245	theorem isOpen_setOf_hasWitnessH1Vanishing_testPointField
   246	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom) {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]

     9	/-!
    10	# C9b: `IsChartUniv` reduced to one clause about the chart locus
    11	
    12	`Picard/Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean` splits `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` into the two
    13	clauses mathlib's `MorphismProperty.relative` actually conjoins, and gives a criterion whose
    14	input is elementwise.  This file instantiates that criterion at the Abel chart and at
    15	`V := chartLocus`, which is the pair `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes.
    16	
    17	The point is to make the residue **one named clause about the chart locus** instead of the
    18	whole certificate.  Concretely, the criterion's `ChartFibrePresented` datum has four fields,
    19	and at the Abel chart three of them are supplied here:
    20	
    21	| field | at the Abel chart | status |
    22	|---|---|---|
    23	| `W` | `chartLocus` of the test point's class, as an open | **shape supplied here**, but at the
    24	  cost of `haff` — see the retraction below |
    25	| `r` | the divisor family over the locus | the classifier `divRepClassifyZar` |
    26	| `sq` | its class is the test's class | the classifier's own characterisation |
    27	| `exists_factor` | uniqueness of the normalized representative | **the relative form of GAP-2** |
    28	
    29	So `W` needs only B-4 (**not** "nothing" — retracted below), `sq` is a property of whatever
    30	`r` is, and the genuine content is
    31	concentrated in `r` (a construction, from the classifier) and `exists_factor` (relative
    32	GAP-2).  This file makes that split machine-checkable: `IsChartLocusFibre` below names
    33	exactly the `r`/`sq`/`exists_factor` triple **at the chart locus**, and
    34	`isChartUniv_of_isChartLocusFibre` proves `IsChartUniv` from it.
    35	
    36	## Why this is not a restatement
    37	
    38	A reduction that merely renames its obligation is worthless, and this one is checked against
    39	that failure mode in two directions:
    40	
    41	* `chartLocusOpens` is **constructed**, not hypothesised, so the `W` field is a *shape* a lane
    42	  no longer has to invent.
    43	
    44	  **RETRACTED 2026-07-29, second clause only** (`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageAbel.lean`).  This
    45	  read "the `W` field costs zero, which is a real reduction of the datum from four fields to
    46	  three".  The cost is not zero: `chartLocusOpens` takes the argument `haff`, and **nothing in
    47	  the tree discharges it**.  `isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal'` removed the
    48	  `IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant` hypothesis but passes `haff` straight through, as does
    49	  `isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal` before it; the affine case that would feed it
    50	  (`isOpen_setOf_isSplitWitness_of_presentation`) is itself conditional on
    51	  `IsChartDatumPresentation`, which is dat-b row B-4's named residue and is only half landed.
    52	  So the datum went from four fields to three *shapes* but not to three *obligations*.  The
    53	  residue is now named `ChartLocusAffineLocal` and reduced to B-4's own obligation by
    54	  `chartLocusAffineLocal_of_presentation`;
    55	* `isChartLocusFibre_of_isChartUniv` is the **converse**: `IsChartUniv` at the chart locus
    56	  gives injectivity on every test, so a lane cannot obtain `IsChartUniv` while avoiding the
    57	  content of `exists_factor`.  The reduction is therefore an equivalence in the direction
    58	  that matters, not a weakening.
    59	
    60	## Main declarations
    61	
    62	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartLocusOpens` — `chartLocus` as an honest `T.Opens`, using the
    63	  unconditional general-test openness.  This is the `V` that `restrictChart` wants.
    64	* `AlgebraicGeometry.IsChartLocusFibre` — the residue: the `r`/`sq`/`exists_factor` triple
    65	  of the criterion, at the chart locus, for every test point.
    66	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isChartUniv_of_isChartLocusFibre` — **the reduction**: that triple
    67	  gives `IsChartUniv` (hence the `hf` of the `(f, hf)` pair) at any open.
    68	* `AlgebraicGeometry.injective_of_isChartUniv` — the converse-direction check.
    69	-/

    87	/-! ## The chart locus as an open of the test
    88

    97	/-- **`chartLocus` as an open subscheme of the test.**
    98	
    99	For a test `T` presented as `Over.mk a` and a class `lam` on it, the chart locus is open by
   100	`isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal'` (CHART-U(b) at a general test, unconditional since
   101	`IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant` was discharged), so it is an honest element of `T.Opens`.
   102	
   103	**THE `haff` SENTENCE HERE WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED** (2026-07-29,
   104	`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageAbel.lean`).  It read: "The `haff` hypothesis is the affine-local
   105	input of that theorem and is *not* a residue of this file: it is what the landed affine
   106	openness supplies."  The landed affine openness does **not** supply it.
   107	`isOpen_setOf_isSplitWitness_of_presentation` (`Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen.lean:321`) is conditional
   108	on `IsChartDatumPresentation` — dat-b row B-4's own named residue, whose *witness* half is now

   113	`chartLocusAffineLocal_of_presentation`.  It is
   114	carried as an argument here so the definition does not silently depend on a chosen route. -/
   115	def chartLocusOpens (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
   116	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (lam : picEt C T)
   117	    (haff : ∀ U : T.left.affineOpens,
   118	      IsOpen (chartLocus C m Z (picEtMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) lam))) :

   125	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {lam : picEt C T}
   126	    {haff : ∀ U : T.left.affineOpens,
   127	      IsOpen (chartLocus C m Z (picEtMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) lam))}
   128	    {t : T.left} :

   134	variable (C π n) in
   135	/-- **The residue of C9b, named**: for every test point of the Σ-sheaf, the chart point over
   136	its chart locus together with the two properties the criterion needs.
   137	
   138	**THE NEXT SENTENCE WAS FALSE AND IS RETRACTED (2026-07-29,
   139	`Picard/Pic0ChartLocusFibreGuard.lean`).**  It read: "This is `ChartFibrePresented` with its
   140	`W` field already discharged — it is `chartLocus`, open unconditionally".  The `W` field is
   141	**free**: it is a field of the structure, quantified inside the `Nonempty` below, and
   142	`chartLocus` occurs nowhere in this definition — nor does `chartLocus` or `V` enter the proof
   143	of `isChartUniv_of_isChartLocusFibre`.  The criterion consumes the datum for the
   144	**unrestricted** chart, so this statement implies
   145	`IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (abelSigmaChart …)` at `V = ⊤`, hence `Mono`, hence injectivity on
   146	every test — which `Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean:54`, `Pic0ChartPair.lean:14` and
   147	`Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean:214` all cite as FALSE for the Abel chart (its fibres

   150	See `not_isChartLocusFibre_of_not_injective` for the guard instantiated here, and inbox
   151	`I-0874`.  A lane must decide that fork before attacking `exists_factor`.
   152	
   153	Modulo that retraction, what a lane owes is:
   154	
   155	* `r`: the divisor family over the locus whose class is the given one.  This is the
   156	  classifier `divRepClassifyZar` applied to the canonical-section family, i.e. CHART-U(c)'s
   157	  construction;
   158	* `sq`: that its chart value *is* the given class, which is the classifier's characterising

   160	* `exists_factor`: that two points with the same class agree, i.e. the **relative form of
   161	  DAT-C GAP-2** (`Scheme.CurveDivisor.eq_of_picClass_eq_of_h0_one` in families).
   162	
   163	Stated as a `Prop` over an arbitrary presenting datum rather than as a structure carrying the
   164	family, because the family is the classifier's output and this lane must not guess its shape:
   165	the existential is over morphisms of schemes only. -/
   166	def IsChartLocusFibre {D : Over (Spec (.of k))} (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
   167	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
   168	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
   169	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ)) : Prop :=
   170	  ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1),
   171	    Nonempty (ChartFibrePresented C (abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg) g)
   172	
   173	/-- **THE REDUCTION**: the residue above gives `IsChartUniv`, hence the `hf` of the `(f, hf)`
   174	pair, at *any* open of the divisor scheme.
   175	
   176	Two things are worth reading off the proof.  First, it goes through the criterion of
   177	`Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean` and then through the *composition* half
   178	`isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart` already landed in `Pic0ChartPair.lean` — so the two
   179	halves of C9b compose exactly as the file headers predicted, with no seam.  Second, the open
   180	`V` is arbitrary: restriction never has to be to the chart locus for `hf` to hold, because
   181	`IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` is stable under precomposition with an open immersion.  The chart
   182	locus is where the *unrestricted* statement becomes true, which is a statement about
   183	`IsChartLocusFibre`, not about `V`. -/
   184	theorem isChartUniv_of_isChartLocusFibre {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   185	    (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
   186	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
   187	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
   188	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
   189	    (h : IsChartLocusFibre C π n rep m Z hdeg) (V : D.left.Opens) :
   190	    IsChartUniv C π n rep m Z hdeg V :=
   191	  isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart V
   192	    (isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented _ fun T g => (h T g).some)
   193	
   194	/-! ## The converse check: the reduction is not a weakening -/
   195	
   196	/-- **`IsChartUniv` forces elementwise injectivity of the restricted chart.**
   197	
   198	The converse direction of the reduction, and the reason it is a reduction rather than a
   199	restatement: a lane that obtains `IsChartUniv` has, for free, the injectivity statement that
   200	`ChartFibrePresented.exists_factor` is the hard half of.  So there is no route to `hf` that
   201	avoids relative GAP-2 — the gate is real, and this file has moved it rather than removed it.
   202	
   203	Compare `isEmpty_forall_chartFibrePresented_of_not_injective`: that says the criterion cannot
   204	be *satisfied* without injectivity; this says the goal cannot be *reached* without it. -/
   205	theorem injective_of_isChartUniv {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   206	    (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
   207	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
   208	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
   209	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
   210	    (V : D.left.Opens) (h : IsChartUniv C π n rep m Z hdeg V) (T : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ) :
   211	    Function.Injective ((restrictChart (abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg) V).app T) :=
   212	  injective_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf h T

   583	/-- A rank-one presentation has a tied local-away evaluation generator.
   584	
   585	The rank-one field of `P` makes every residue-field fibre of its `H⁰` module nontrivial.
   586	The projective-module generator lemma therefore supplies a single basic open `D(f)` and
   587	one datum section `y` which stays nonzero on every residue fibre over that open.  The same
   588	`y` is transported to a native global section and its unit-lift through the evaluation
   589	counit; the final conjunct records that counit identity explicitly so the future
   590	`divisorOfRankOne` construction consumes this witness rather than an unrelated section.

   593	    (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   594	    (p : PrimeSpectrum P.cover.Carrier) :
   595	    ∃ f : P.cover.Carrier, f ∉ p.asIdeal ∧
   596	      ∃ y : Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0,
   597	        (∀ q : PrimeSpectrum P.cover.Carrier, f ∉ q.asIdeal →
   598	          (y ⊗ₜ (1 : q.asIdeal.ResidueField) :
   599	            Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0 ⊗[P.cover.Carrier]
   600	              q.asIdeal.ResidueField) ≠ 0) ∧
   601	        (Scheme.Modules.Hom.app P.evaluation
   602	          ((relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier)) ⁻¹ᵁ
   603	            (⊤ : (Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier)).Opens))).hom
   604	          (P.evaluationLiftOfH0 y) = P.pushforwardSectionOfH0 y := by
   605	  let Q := Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0
   606	  letI : Module.Finite P.cover.Carrier Q := P.h0_finite
   607	  letI : Module.Projective P.cover.Carrier Q := P.h0_projective
   608	  have hfr : Module.finrank p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   609	      (p.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[P.cover.Carrier] Q) = 1 := by
   610	    rw [← Module.rankAtStalk_eq]
   611	    exact P.h0_rank_one p
   612	  haveI : Nontrivial (p.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[P.cover.Carrier] Q) :=
   613	    Module.nontrivial_of_finrank_pos (by rw [hfr]; norm_num)
   614	  haveI : Nontrivial (Q ⊗[P.cover.Carrier] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :=
   615	    (TensorProduct.comm P.cover.Carrier _ _).toEquiv.symm.nontrivial
   616	  obtain ⟨f, hf, y, hy⟩ :=
   617	    Module.exists_fibrewise_tmul_ne_zero_of_projective p (Q := Q)
   618	      (by infer_instance)
   619	  refine ⟨f, hf, y, ?_, ?_⟩
   620	  · simpa only [Q] using hy
   621	  · exact P.evaluation_evaluationLiftOfH0 y

   701	identify that class with `representative`, rewrite it as the datum's relative Picard class,

   703	theorem datum_classDeg_baseChange
   704	    (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   705	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra P.cover.Carrier L]
   706	    [IsScalarTower k P.cover.Carrier L] :

   709	        P.datum.cechPicClass) = genus C := by

   711	    (Algebra.ofId A P.cover.Carrier).restrictScalars k
   712	  let psi : P.cover.Carrier →ₐ[k] L :=
   713	    (Algebra.ofId P.cover.Carrier L).restrictScalars k
   714	  have hcurve :
   715	      relCurveMap C P.cover.Carrier L =
   716	        (C ◁ Over.overSpecMap psi).left := by
   717	    refine congrArg
   718	      (fun f : overSpec k L ⟶ overSpec k P.cover.Carrier => (C ◁ f).left) ?_
   719	    exact Over.OverMorphism.ext rfl
   720	  have hpresentation :
   721	      picEtMap C (Over.overSpecMap iota) lam.1 =
   722	        relPicToPicEt C (overSpec k P.cover.Carrier)
   723	          (P.representative : relPic C (overSpec k P.cover.Carrier)) := by
   724	    exact picEtMap_eq_relPicToPicEt_of_affineRepresentative
   725	      C lam.1 P.cover P.representative P.represents.symm
   726	  calc
   727	    classDeg L
   728	        (Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C P.cover.Carrier L)
   729	          P.datum.cechPicClass) =
   730	      relPicDeg L
   731	        (relPicMk C (overSpec k L)
   732	          (Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C P.cover.Carrier L)
   733	            P.datum.cechPicClass)) :=
   734	      (relPicDeg_relPicMk L _).symm
   735	    _ = relPicDeg L
   736	        (relPicMap C (Over.overSpecMap psi)
   737	          (relPicMk C (overSpec k P.cover.Carrier)
   738	            P.datum.cechPicClass)) := by
   739	      rw [relPicMap_mk, ← hcurve]
   740	      rfl
   741	    _ = relPicDeg L
   742	        (relPicMap C (Over.overSpecMap psi)
   743	          (P.representative : relPic C (overSpec k P.cover.Carrier))) := by
   744	      rw [P.datum_class]
   745	    _ = degAt
   746	        (relPicToPicEt C (overSpec k P.cover.Carrier)
   747	          (P.representative : relPic C (overSpec k P.cover.Carrier)))
   748	        (Over.overSpecMap psi) :=
   749	      (degAt_relPicToPicEt
   750	        (P.representative : relPic C (overSpec k P.cover.Carrier))
   751	        (Over.overSpecMap psi)).symm
   752	    _ = degAt (picEtMap C (Over.overSpecMap iota) lam.1)
   753	        (Over.overSpecMap psi) := by rw [hpresentation]
   754	    _ = degAt lam.1 (Over.overSpecMap psi ≫ Over.overSpecMap iota) :=
   755	      degAt_picEtMap (Over.overSpecMap iota) lam.1 (Over.overSpecMap psi)
   756	    _ = genus C := lam.2 L (Over.overSpecMap psi ≫ Over.overSpecMap iota)

    16	/-!
    17	# The local-presentation contract for the rank-one Picard locus
    18	
    19	An element of `picDegLayerFunctor` is an etale-plus class, not a chosen line bundle.  The
    20	rank-one route therefore needs an explicit local presentation before it can use the evaluation
    21	map of a line bundle.  `PicRankOneLocalPresentation` records that presentation on an affine
    22	test and ties every piece of data to the input class:
    23	
    24	* a descent-class representative whose plus class is the affine collapse of the input;
    25	* a cocycle datum presenting that same relative Picard class;
    26	* a locally free rank-one `Scheme.Modules` object whose base-ring sheaf is the datum's sheaf;
    27	* invertibility of the canonical native pushforward base-change mate on every cartesian square;
    28	* the cohomological rank-one outputs used by the evaluation construction.
    29	
    30	No existence, openness, or representability assertion is made here.  The first canonical
    31	consumer is `PicRankOneLocalPresentation.evaluation`, the pullback-pushforward counit.
    32	The method `PicRankOneLocalPresentation.h0BaseChange` derives arbitrary affine base change
    33	from the same presentation's `H^1`-vanishing field.  The section bridge at the end identifies
    34	datum `H^0` with native global sections and proves, by the adjunction triangle identity, that
    35	the evaluation counit sends the canonical unit-lift back to that same section.
    36	-/

   131	noncomputable def nativeBaseChangeIso (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   132	    {T' X' : Scheme.{u}}
   133	    (g : T' ⟶ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier)) (f' : X' ⟶ T')
   134	    (g' : X' ⟶ relCurve C P.cover.Carrier)

   147	    [IsScalarTower k P.cover.Carrier B] :

import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.ThetaDegree

/-!
# The translated rank-one cover brick

This file records the part of the separably-closed cover argument that is already consumable by
the landed fibre API.  A `BaseFieldTranslationDrop` keeps the input class `lambda` in the
presentation equation, chooses its base-field translating class explicitly, and records the
positive-twist/point-subtraction output.  The consumer below turns that output into the exact
`IsSplitWitness` shape used by `chartLocus`.

The arbitrary-affine family of `PicRankOneLocalPresentation` objects required by
`PicRankOneOpen` is deliberately not inferred from `h0 = 1` and `H1 = 0`: no such producer is
landed in the current API.  The final theorem therefore exposes the field-level consumer and
keeps that family producer as an explicit integration obligation.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
open TopologicalSpace Opposite

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

open AlgebraicJacobian

attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

noncomputable section

/-! ## The positive-twist input -/

section PositiveTwist

variable {K : Type u} [Field K] {Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral Y]
  [Y.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
  [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
  [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (Y.moduleKSheaf K) 0)]
  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (Y.moduleKSheaf K) 1)]

/-- The FLV class theorem in the spelling used by the translated-cover lane.

The class `l` is the presenting class of the input fibre, while `theta` is the positive
base-field twist.  Keeping this as a named wrapper makes the positive-twist step visible at the
call site; it does not manufacture a presentation or hide the input class in an unrelated
existential. -/
theorem exists_positive_twist_vanishing
    (π : Y ⟶ P1 K) [IsFinite π] [IsDominant π]
    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap K = Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))
    (l θ : Y.CechPic) (hθ : 1 ≤ classDeg K θ) :
    ∃ n₀ : ℕ, ∀ n ≥ n₀, ∀ W : Y.CurveDivisor,
      Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass K W = l * θ ^ n →
        Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K W) 1) := by
  exact exists_subsingleton_hModule_one_of_one_le_classDeg_of_isFinite_toP1
    π hπ l θ hθ

end PositiveTwist

/-! ## The lambda-tied drop package -/

section DropPackage

variable {K L : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
  [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra K L] [IsScalarTower k K L]
  [Module.Finite K L] [Algebra.IsSeparable K L]

/-- Data for the positive twist and the subsequent point subtraction.

`hM₀` ties the splitting field presentation to the particular input `mu`; `hW₀` says that the
divisor being reduced is in the positive twist class (the chart index is zero at this stage).
`baseSubtraction` is intentionally an explicit class-level bridge: it says that the divisor
returned by the greedy reduction is represented by a base-field divisor.  The current tree has
the graph-class version of this bridge but no divisor pullback operation, so this hypothesis is
kept visible rather than replaced by a fieldwise existential. -/
structure SepClosedTranslatedDropData (μ : picEt C (overSpec k K)) where
  m : ℕ
  M₀ : (relCurve C L).CechPic
  hM₀ : PicEtAff.map C L (picEtAffineEquiv C K μ) =
    PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M₀)
  W₀ : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor
  hW₀ : Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W₀ =
    M₀ * Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L)
      (chartTwistClass C m (0 : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor))
  genusValue : ℕ
  excess : ℕ
  hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (genusValue : ℤ)
  hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L W₀ = (genusValue : ℤ) + excess
  h1 : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
    ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W₀) 1)
  P : Set ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left)
  hdense : ∀ U : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).Opens,
    (U : Set ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left)).Nonempty → (P ∩ U).Nonempty
  hPcl : ∀ x ∈ P, x ≠ genericPoint ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left)
  hPdeg : ∀ x ∈ P, ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).residueDeg L x = 1
  baseSubtraction : ∀ (S : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor),
    0 ≤ S → Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L S = (excess : ℤ) →
      (∀ (x : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left) (hx : x ≠ genericPoint _),
        coeffAt hx S ≠ 0 → x ∈ P) →
      ∃ Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor,
        Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L S =
          Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L)
            ((chartTwistClass C 0 Z)⁻¹)

/-- The output of the positive-twist/drop construction, tied to both the input class and the
base-field translating divisor.

The final field is the existing fibre consumer.  In particular, `S` is not merely a divisor
with the right cohomology: `baseClass` identifies its class with the base change of `Z`, and
`translated` is about `mu` translated by the resulting base-field class
`chartTwistClass C d.m Z`. -/
structure SepClosedTranslatedDropResult (μ : picEt C (overSpec k K))
    (d : SepClosedTranslatedDropData (C := C) (L := L) μ) where
  S : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor
  Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor
  nonnegative : 0 ≤ S
  degree : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L S = (d.excess : ℤ)
  support : ∀ (x : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left) (hx : x ≠ genericPoint _),
    coeffAt hx S ≠ 0 → x ∈ d.P
  baseClass : Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L S =
    Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L) ((chartTwistClass C 0 Z)⁻¹)
  h0_one : Sheaf.h0
    ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L (d.W₀ - S)) = 1
  h1_vanishing : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
    ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L (d.W₀ - S)) 1)
  translated : IsSplitWitness C
    (μ * thetaFamily C (chartTwistClass C d.m Z) (overSpec k K))

/-- Positive twisting followed by point subtraction produces the exact field-level translated
rank-one witness.

The greedy theorem supplies `S`, `h0 = 1`, and preservation of `H1 = 0`.  The explicit
`baseSubtraction` bridge then supplies the base divisor `Z`; class arithmetic shows that
`W₀ - S` presents `mu` translated by the base-field class `chartTwistClass C d.m Z`.  The last
line applies the existing `IsSplitWitness` consumer, so no unrelated Picard class can satisfy
the conclusion. -/
theorem exists_sepClosedTranslatedDropResult
    (μ : picEt C (overSpec k K))
    (d : SepClosedTranslatedDropData (C := C) (L := L) μ) :
    Nonempty (SepClosedTranslatedDropResult (C := C) (L := L) μ d) := by
  obtain ⟨-, S, hS0, hSdeg, hSsupport, hS0one, hS1⟩ :=
    exists_isSplitWitness_of_drop C μ d.m
      (0 : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
      d.genusValue d.excess d.hχ d.M₀ d.hM₀ d.W₀ d.hW₀ d.hdeg d.h1
      d.P d.hdense d.hPcl d.hPdeg
  obtain ⟨Z, hSZ⟩ := d.baseSubtraction S hS0 hSdeg hSsupport
  have hW : Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L (d.W₀ - S) =
      d.M₀ * Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L)
        (chartTwistClass C d.m Z) := by
    have hW₀ := d.hW₀
    unfold relCurveMap relCurve at hW₀ hSZ ⊢
    rw [sub_eq_add_neg, Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass_add, Scheme.picClass_neg,
      hW₀, hSZ]
    simp only [map_inv, inv_inv]
    rw [mul_assoc, ← map_mul]
    simp only [chartTwistClass, Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass_zero, inv_one, mul_one,
      pow_zero, one_mul]
  have htranslated : IsSplitWitness C
      (μ * thetaFamily C (chartTwistClass C d.m Z) (overSpec k K)) :=
    isSplitWitness_of_witness_twistClass C μ d.m Z d.M₀ d.hM₀
      (d.W₀ - S) hW hS1
  exact ⟨{
    S := S
    Z := Z
    nonnegative := hS0
    degree := hSdeg
    support := hSsupport
    baseClass := hSZ
    h0_one := hS0one
    h1_vanishing := hS1
    translated := htranslated
  }⟩

end DropPackage

end

end AlgebraicGeometry
